questions.question: The Ramsar Convention is the intergovernmental treaty that provides the framework for the conservation of _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__option 4.__**

Answer: 

 
• The Ramsar Convention, formally named the **Convention on Wetlands of International Importance** Especially as Waterfowl Habitat, is an international treaty established in **1971 **in the Iranian city of Ramsar.
 
• It aims for the **conservation and wise use of wetlands.**

**​Objectives:**

 
• 
 
To halt the worldwide loss of wetlands and to conserve, through wise use and management, those that remain.To promote the wise use of wetlands in their entirety, through the formulation and implementation of plans for the wise use of wetland resources. To establish nature reserves on wetlands, whether they are governmental or private, so as to provide for their conservation.

questions.question: How many members were there in the drafting committee of Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
**__Answer : (3)__ - 7 - **The seven-member of the Drafting Committee headed by B.R. Ambedkar were- N. Gopalswami Aiyengar, Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar, K.M. Munshi, Mohammad Saadullah, B.L. Mittar (replaced by N. Madhav Rau later) and D.P Khaitan (replaced by T.T. Krishnamachari).

 
• The Drafting Committee was one of the **22 committees** formed to facilitate the work of Constitution-making.
 
• The Drafting Committee finalized the draft in February 1948 and the second reading was completed on October 17, 1948. The third reading was done on Nov. 14, 1949.
 
• The Constitution was adopted on November, 26,1949.

questions.question: Green revolution is related to _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Production of wheat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Green Revolution** refers to a period when Indian agriculture was converted into an industrial system due to the adoption of modern methods and technologies such as the use of **High Yielding Variety Seeds**, irrigation facilities, pesticides, and fertilizers.
 
• **M.S. Swaminathan** is considered the "Father of Green Revolution" in India.
 
• **HYV **seeds were developed by Prof. **Norman Borlaug**.
 
• The term **Green Revolution** was first used by **William Gaud** and **Norman Borlaug** is the **Father of the Green Revolution** in the **world**. 
 
• It commenced in 1965 that led to an increase in food grain production (most useful for wheat production), especially in Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh.

questions.question: Khadar is _________.
questions.solution:
**__Answer : (2) __- New Alluvial Soil **- Also known as the Khadar soil, it has been formed by the deposition of the new Alluvial Soil and is found in the low land.

 
• It becomes fertile by the flood water which reaches the region every year.
 
• Eastern Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and West Bengal consist of mostly the Khadar soil.

questions.question: When was the Central Rural Sanitation Programme launched?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__1986__**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• The Central Rural Sanitation program, launched in 1986 was the first major structured initiative of cleanliness in India. This was launched by the Rajiv Gandhi led Congress government.
 
• The objective of CRSP was to construct individual sanitary latrines for the personal use of the BPL population.
 
• The main reason behind the program was to improve the quality of life of the rural people and provide privacy and dignity to women.
 
• CRSP was restructured to** Total Sanitation Campain (TSC)** from 1999 during the Atal Bihari Vajpayee government. The aim of this campaign was to eradicate open defecation by the year 2010.
 
• **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan** launched by the Modi-led NDA government on October 2, 2014, is a broader and largest program on sanitation by the Indian Government.

questions.question: What is the full form of MOU?
questions.solution:
**__Answer : (1)__ - Memorandum of Understanding** - is a formal agreement between two or more parties. Companies and organizations can use MoUs to establish official partnerships.

 
• MoUs are not legally binding but can be termed as the first steps towards a legal contract.
 
• MoUs are popular in multinational international relations because, unlike treaties, they take a short time to ratify and can be kept confidential.
 
• MoUs may also be used to modify existing treaties.

questions.question: Which micronutrient is supplied by soil to plant?
questions.solution:
**__Answer : (3)__ - Zinc** - is one of the essential micro-nutrient of soil needed for producing **chlorophyll**.

 
• Aids in plant growth.
 
• Improves root development, flowering and fruit production.

 

 
• Plant nutrients from soil :

 
• Primary nutrients - Nitrogen, Phosphorus and Potassium.
 
• Secondary nutrients - Calcium, Magnesium and Sulphur
 
• Micro-nutrients - Boron, Chlorine, Copper, Iron, Magnese, Molybdenum and Zinc.
